Time, Speed & Distance.story_template: A {vehicle_type} travels at {speed} km/h for {time} hours. How many kilometres does it cover?
Two vehicles start {distance_apart} km apart and move directly toward each other at {speed1} km/h and {speed2} km/h. After how many hours will they meet?
Time, Speed & Distance.solution_logic: Compute opposite-direction relative speed, then time = distance / relative speed.

Time, Speed & Distance.story_template: A train {train_length} m long moves at {speed} km/h and must completely cross a platform {platform_length} m long. How many seconds does the crossing take?
Time, Speed & Distance.solution_logic: Add train and platform lengths, convert km/h to m/s, then divide total distance by speed.

Work & Time.story_template: A worker can complete a job alone in {total_time} days. If the worker works at the same rate for {days_worked} days, what percentage of the job is completed?
Work & Time.solution_logic: Use work fraction = days worked / total days and convert to a percentage.

Work & Time.story_template: {person1_name} can complete a task in {person1_time} days and {person2_name} can complete it in {person2_time} days. If they work together at constant rates, how many days will the task take?
Work & Time.solution_logic: Add individual work rates and invert the combined rate.

Work & Time.story_template: Worker A can finish a job in {person1_time} days and worker B in {person2_time} days. They work together for {together_days} days, after which A leaves and B finishes the remaining work alone. How many days in total does the job take?
Work & Time.solution_logic: Compute work done together, subtract from one whole job, then use B's rate for the remainder and add elapsed time.

Pipes & Cisterns.story_template: A pipe can fill an empty tank in {fill_time} hours. If it is left open for {open_hours} hours at the same rate, what percentage of the tank is filled?
Pipes & Cisterns.solution_logic: Use filled fraction = open time / full fill time and convert to a percentage.

Pipes & Cisterns.story_template: Pipe A fills a tank in {pipe1_fill_time} hours and pipe B fills it in {pipe2_fill_time} hours. If both are opened together, how many hours are needed to fill the tank?
Pipes & Cisterns.solution_logic: Add the two inlet rates and invert the net rate.

Pipes & Cisterns.story_template: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank separately in {pipe1_fill_time} hours and {pipe2_fill_time} hours. An outlet can empty a full tank in {outlet_time} hours. If all three are opened together from an empty tank, how many hours will the tank take to fill?
Pipes & Cisterns.solution_logic: Add inlet rates, subtract the outlet rate, verify positive net flow, then invert.

Profit, Loss & Discount.story_template: An {item_type} costs ${cost_price} and is sold for ${selling_price}. What is the profit or loss percentage, measured on cost price?
Profit, Loss & Discount.solution_logic: Find SP − CP, take its magnitude, divide by CP, then convert to a percentage.

Profit, Loss & Discount.story_template: An item is marked at ${marked_price}. A store applies a {discount1}% discount and then an additional {discount2}% discount on the reduced price. What is the final selling price?
Profit, Loss & Discount.solution_logic: Apply the first discount multiplicatively, then apply the second discount to the reduced price.

Profit, Loss & Discount.story_template: A retailer buys an item for ${cost_price}, marks it up by {markup}% and then offers successive discounts of {discount1}% and {discount2}% on the marked price. What is the resulting profit or loss percentage on cost price?
Profit, Loss & Discount.solution_logic: Compute marked price from markup, apply both discounts multiplicatively, then compare final SP with CP and express the difference as a percentage of CP.

Mixtures & Ratio.story_template: A {total_quantity}-liter mixture contains {item1_name} and {item2_name} in the ratio {ratio1}:{ratio2}. How many liters of {item1_name} are present?
Mixtures & Ratio.solution_logic: Take the requested ratio part over total ratio parts and multiply by total quantity.

Mixtures & Ratio.story_template: A mixture contains {item1_name} and {item2_name} in the ratio {initial_ratio_part1}:{initial_ratio_part2}. After {added_quantity} liters of {item1_name} is added, the ratio becomes {final_ratio_part1}:{final_ratio_part2}. What was the initial total quantity of the mixture?
Mixtures & Ratio.solution_logic: Represent initial components with a common multiplier, apply the added amount, then solve the final-ratio equation for the original total.

Mixtures & Ratio.story_template: A vessel contains {vessel_capacity} liters of pure liquid. Each time, {replaced_quantity} liters is removed and replaced with water. This operation is repeated {repetitions} times. How many liters of the original liquid remain?

Age-Based Problems.story_template: {person_name} is currently {current_age} years old. How old will {person_name} be after {years_future} years?
Age-Based Problems.solution_logic: Add the future interval to the current age.

Age-Based Problems.story_template: {person1_name} is {person1_age} years old and {person2_name} is {person2_age} years old. What will be the simplified ratio of their ages after {years_future} years?
Age-Based Problems.solution_logic: Find both future ages and reduce their ratio using the greatest common divisor.

Age-Based Problems.story_template: {older_name} is {age_difference} years older than {younger_name}. After {years_future} years, {older_name} will be {future_multiple} times as old as {younger_name}. What is {younger_name}'s current age?
Age-Based Problems.solution_logic: Form two linked age equations using the constant age difference and the future multiple, then solve backward for the younger person's current age.

Time, Speed & Distance.relative_speed: Must be non-zero for distinct events (e.g., meeting, crossing).
Time, Speed & Distance.boat_speed_still_water: Must be > stream_speed for upstream travel.

Work & Time.work_rate: Must be > 0 (unless specified as destructive work).
Work & Time.combined_time: Must be > 0 and typically less than the smallest individual time (for positive work rates).

Pipes & Cisterns.net_flow_rate: Must be > 0 for filling, < 0 for emptying, and non-zero for a finite solution.

Profit, Loss & Discount.percentage: Profit/Loss/Discount percentages should be in a reasonable range (e.g., typically 0-100% for discounts, and realistic ranges for profit/loss).

Mixtures & Ratio.quantity: Must be > 0 for all components and the total mixture.
Mixtures & Ratio.replacement_quantity: Must be > 0 and less than or equal to the total mixture quantity.

Age-Based Problems.years_past_future: Can be positive (future) or negative (past), but resulting ages must remain positive.

Time, Speed & Distance: Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time
Time for Train to Cross (Length L_T, Speed S_T) a stationary object (Length L_O) = (L_T + L_O) / S_T
Upstream Speed = Boat Speed - Stream Speed
Downstream Speed = Boat Speed + Stream Speed
Work & Time: Combined Rate = Sum of Individual Rates
(M1 * D1 * H1) / W1 = (M2 * D2 * H2) / W2 (Man-Days Formula)
Pipes & Cisterns: Rate of Inlet Pipe = +1 / Time to Fill
Rate of Outlet Pipe = -1 / Time to Empty
Net Flow Rate = Sum of all (Inlet Rates + Outlet Rates)
Time to Fill/Empty Tank = Total Capacity (usually 1 unit) / Net Flow Rate
Profit, Loss & Discount: Equivalent Discount for Successive Discounts D1, D2 = D1 + D2 - (D1 * D2 / 100)
Mixtures & Ratio: Ratio A:B = Quantity A / Quantity B
Quantity of component in new mixture = (Q1*C1 + Q2*C2) / (Q1+Q2)
Alligation Rule: Ratio of quantities Q1/Q2 = (C2 - Cm) / (Cm - C1) where C is concentration and Cm is mean concentration.
Replacement Formula: Final Quantity of a component = Initial Quantity * (1 - Replaced Volume / Total Volume)^n (where n is number of replacements)
Age-Based Problems: Age in Future = Current Age + Years
Age in Past = Current Age - Years
Difference in ages between two people remains constant over time.
Sum of ages changes by (Number of people * Years) over time.
Solve using linear equations based on given ratios or differences.

Time, Speed & Distance: Negative or zero values for speed, time, or distance.
Boat speed in still water is less than or equal to stream speed when moving upstream.
Time taken to cover a positive distance is zero.
Work & Time: Negative or zero time for an individual or group to complete a task.
A combined positive work rate results in infinite time (e.g., one person's positive rate cancelled by another's negative rate exactly).
One person 'completes' work in less than zero days.
Pipes & Cisterns: Negative or zero time for a pipe to fill or empty.
Total inflow rate is less than or equal to total outflow rate when the problem expects the tank to be filled.
Tank capacity is negative or zero.
Profit, Loss & Discount: Negative or zero Cost Price (CP), Selling Price (SP), or Marked Price (MP).
Discount percentage exceeding 100% (implies paying the customer).
Profit/Loss percentage resulting in an impossible SP (e.g., negative SP).
Mixtures & Ratio: Negative or zero quantity for any liquid or component.
Ratio parts being zero or negative.
Attempting to remove more liquid than present in the mixture.
Age-Based Problems: Resulting age for any person is negative or zero.
Contradictory age statements (e.g., A is older than B, but B's age in the future becomes greater than A's, contradicting the age difference).
A person's age is decreasing over time (unless specified for a specific context like biological age vs. calendar age).

mcq_distractor_rules: Arithmetic slips (e.g., addition instead of subtraction, incorrect multiplication/division).
Swapped values (e.g., using A's efficiency for B, upstream for downstream speed).
Incorrect unit conversion (e.g., not converting hours to minutes, km/h to m/s).
Wrong percentage base (e.g., calculating profit/loss percentage on SP instead of CP).
Incorrect ratio application (e.g., inverting the ratio, calculating one part instead of the total).
Wrong relative speed direction (e.g., adding speeds for same direction, subtracting for opposite).
Incorrect mixture replacement formula application (e.g., forgetting exponent 'n').
Ignoring specific problem conditions (e.g., a pipe closing midway, a worker leaving).
Calculating an intermediate value instead of the final requested answer.
Common misconceptions or simplified approaches (e.g., averaging times in work & time problems instead of using rates).
